title: Quentin and the Asset
premise: Odile Winterbourne, a private security contractor who has spent two decades making herself unmemorable, receives a debt notice from a stranger named Quentin Voss claiming she once saved his life—a favor she has no memory of doing. The 'interest' on that debt is a stolen dossier that three governments and a professional assassin named Marrow will kill to bury, and Quentin insists Odile is the only person with the clearance history to move it safely. As they run from Vienna to the Baltic coast, Odile discovers the favor was real: she saved a boy during a mission her employers erased from her memory, and the boy was Quentin. The dossier contains proof that the agency she still works for traffics in erased people like her, and the ending comes when Odile chooses to detonate her own carefully invisible life—exposing the agency, losing her career, and gaining, for the first time, a family that chose her back.
about_author: J. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent eleven years moving sensitive cargo through Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town in Maine, where they are rumored to keep an unread dossier in a fireproof box.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In Vienna, Odile finishes a routine protection detail and finds a stranger, Quentin Voss, waiting in her apartment with a debt notice for a favor she doesn't remember. He knows details of her erased past no one should have. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in twenty years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Quentin reveals the 'interest': an encrypted dossier proving their shared employer, Halcyon Group, erases people—identities, memories, records—and repurposes them. Before Odile can refuse, an attempt on Quentin's life forces them to flee together. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born under fire.

chapters.title: Marrow
chapters.summary: POV Marrow. The assassin Marrow receives the contract: two names, no timeline, discretion absolute. We see his meticulous, almost tender professionalism as he reconstructs Odile's hidden history. Emotional beat: cold dread—the reader learns how good the hunter is.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV Odile. On a night train to Prague, Odile tests the dossier against her own memories and finds gaps exactly where Quentin says the erasures fall. She contacts an old handler and gets a warning that confirms the rot. Emotional beat: grief—the life she trusted was a constructed thing.

chapters.title: The Boy on the Pier
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin recalls Riga, 2004: a child hiding under a pier while a young contractor held off shooters until dawn. He has spent twenty years finding her. He tells Odile the truth of who she saved, and who he is. Emotional beat: recognition—the debt was always love in disguise.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Assassin
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In Prague, a Halcyon fixer offers Odile reinstatement and a clean record if she surrenders Quentin and the dossier. She stalls, and Marrow nearly takes them both in the exchange. Emotional beat: temptation and refusal—she chooses the stranger over the institution.

chapters.title: Safe Houses and Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A network of people Odile once protected—now a smuggler, a nurse, a forger—shelter the pair without being asked, repaying old debts. Quentin watches Odile realize she built a family she never counted. Emotional beat: warmth—the found family assembles itself.

chapters.title: The Baltic Option
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Cornered in Gdańsk, they plan to route the dossier through a defected archivist who can authenticate it past three governments' firewalls. Marrow intercepts the archivist; the plan bleeds. Emotional beat: desperation—time runs out as the window closes.

chapters.title: What Marrow Was Owed
chapters.summary: POV Marrow, then Odile. Confrontation on a cargo ship: Marrow reveals he too was erased by Halcyon, his contract a leash. Odile offers him the dossier instead of a fight. He lets them pass—and turns the contract inward. Emotional beat: the assassin's humanity; the climax pivots on mercy.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The dossier goes public; Halcyon burns, and Odile's own record is un-erased at last—her real name restored. She declines every offer of a new career, choosing instead the loose, imperfect family from chapter seven. Final beat: quiet resolution—she is visible, known, and home.
